source_links.title: What is the evidence for abdominal and pelvic floor muscle training to treat diastasis recti abdominis postpartum? An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials and trial sequential analysis

finding: 15 eligible studies, 803 participants overall; only 3 sufficiently similar studies contributed to pooled TrA-focused exercise vs minimal/no intervention. MD −0.06 cm (95% CI −1.19 to 1.08), p=.92.
limitations: Considerable heterogeneity, pooled sample not available from abstract, full text paywalled. Not proof that all exercise is ineffective; anatomical distance is distinct from strength, function or symptoms.

source_links.title: An evidence-based comparison of rehabilitation strategies for diastasis recti abdominis in postpartum women: a systematic review and network meta-analysis

finding: 27 RCTs, 1340 participants, 39 interventions; 26 studies in main network. 42 pairwise comparisons, only 2 replicated in more than one study. 17 low risk, 8 high risk, 2 unclear per authors. Highest ranked TCMEB+KT estimate had low confidence; very early initiation raises natural-recovery concern. Other selected combinations rated higher confidence by authors.
limitations: Indirect comparisons and sparse replication; no independent pooled comparison with Lyons; different intervention definitions and timing; not a safety or functional outcome ranking. SUCRA is a ranking metric, not probability of individual success. Authors could not search EMBASE, CINAHL, PEDro. No claim that individual components independently work.
locator: Publisher abstract, Results, Strengths and limitations, Funding, Competing interest

source_links.title: Topical preparations for preventing stretch marks in pregnancy | Cochrane

disposition: already extracted; clarify dates and denominator
finding: Original review published 2012, search ended Oct 31 2011; 6 studies/800 total, 5 studies/474 for incidence RR .74 (.53–1.03), I² 65%.
limitations: Summary site date does not demonstrate refreshed search. Existing O001 retained, not duplicated. Heterogeneous formulations; no clear pooled prevention benefit.

source_links.title: Prophylaxis of Striae gravidarum with a topical formulation. A double blind trial
Topical preparations for preventing stretch marks in pregnancy | Cochrane

finding: Combination cream 14/41 vs vehicle 22/39 analyzed/valid cases. Trial reports severity means 1.42 (SD .5) vs 2.13 (SD 1.32), p=.014, using nonvalidated 0–3 score; exact severity analysis denominator not known.
limitations: Randomized totals not stated in Cochrane extraction; no funding identified by reviewers, not verified absence. Multiple ingredients, small trial, subgroup and adverse-event details incomplete; no isolated Centella effect.
locator: Primary abstract; Cochrane Characteristics of included studies, Mallol 1991 (indexed excerpt)

source_links.title: Use of a specific anti-stretch mark cream for preventing or reducing the severity of striae gravidarum. Randomized, double-blind, controlled trial

disposition: existing trial; subgroup precision and severity expansion
finding: Overall incidence 37.6% vs 33.3% treated/control, not significant. No prior striae subgroup 5.6% vs 35%, reported OR 9.2 (95% CI 1.0–83.3), p=.031; direction corresponds to higher odds in control. New-striae severity change control .47 (SD .57) vs treatment .14 (SD .60), p=.031. Previous-striae severity increase 17.8% control vs 6.3% treated; within-group significance is not direct between-group evidence.
limitations: Subgroup denominator, pre-specification, complete harms and funding not extracted; extremely wide CI; no ingredient isolation. Preserve reported OR direction, do not relabel as treatment/control. Not evidence of routine prevention.

source_links.title: Postpartum stretchmarks: repairing activity of an oral Centella asiatica supplementation (Centellicum®)
European Union herbal monograph on Centella asiatica (L.) Urb., herba, revision 1

disposition: new study and safety reference; research-only candidate
finding: 78 healthy participants at least 6 months postpartum; 25 used branded topical cream, 28 hydrating control, 25 hydrating cream plus oral Centella. Six weeks; authors report better instrument and appearance outcomes with combination and no observed side effects.
limitations: Comparative registry, randomization/blinding not established, multiple outcomes, absolute effect sizes unavailable, funding/COI and lactation status unknown. No general safety or causal benefit. EMA cutaneous monograph section 4.6 advises against covered medicinal use in pregnancy/lactation due to inadequate data; does not directly establish oral risk.
locator: PubMed and publisher abstract; EMA section 4.6 p6 (image inspected)

Maternal and foetal cardiovascular responses to moderate-to-high intensity resistance exercise
Pushing limits: acute heavy-load resistance and supine exercise fetal well-being
Impact of heavy resistance training on pregnancy and postpartum health outcomes
